questions.question: Besides its own state or props changing, what else causes a component to re-render?
options: Nothing else — only its own state/props changes trigger a re-render
Its parent re-rendering, even if the child's own props look unchanged
Only a manual call to forceUpdate()
questions.explanation: React re-renders a whole subtree by default when a parent re-renders, regardless of whether a given child's props actually changed.

questions.question: What does `React.memo` do?
options: Caches the result of an expensive function call
Skips re-rendering a component if a shallow comparison finds none of its props changed
Prevents a component from ever re-rendering
questions.explanation: React.memo shallow-compares the new props to the previous ones and bails out of re-rendering if they're equal.

questions.question: Why can `useCallback` be necessary alongside `React.memo`?
options: React.memo doesn't work at all without useCallback
A new inline function is created on every parent render, which breaks React.memo's shallow prop comparison on the child
It's needed to satisfy the Rules of Hooks
questions.explanation: Without useCallback, a function prop is a new reference every render, so a memoized child sees its onClick prop as 'changed' even though the behavior is identical.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach before reaching for useMemo/useCallback everywhere?
options: Apply them to every function and computed value by default
Identify an actual slow render or expensive calculation first, e.g. via the DevTools Profiler
Avoid using them at all, ever
Only use them in class components
questions.explanation: Memoization hooks add their own overhead and complexity; they should be applied to a measured bottleneck, not sprinkled everywhere preemptively.
